title: Sample Paper: Graph-Aware Token Pruning for Code Models
abstract: We exploit the abstract syntax tree of source code to prune redundant tokens before they enter a code language model, reducing FLOPs by 38% with no measurable drop on HumanEval.

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Code language models tokenize source as text, ignoring rich syntactic structure already known to compilers.
We argue that AST traversal order and node typing carry strong cues for which tokens can be dropped.

sections.heading: Method
paragraphs: We parse code with tree-sitter and assign each token an importance score from its AST node type.
Low-importance tokens are merged with neighbors via attention-pooling before the first transformer block.

sections.heading: Experiments
paragraphs: On HumanEval, pass@1 changes from 36.2 to 35.9, well within seed variance.
Throughput improves 1.6x on long completions; FLOPs are reduced by 38%.
